proof_attempt_summary: The run derived a union-honest adaptive interval, a conditional Gaussian-coordinate lower bound, and a theorem showing that a consistent common-fit selector forces the proposed cross-branch bounded-chi-square priors apart. The interval proof also omitted the selected-but-disjoint fallback contribution; a singleton fallback repairs that local issue, but cannot supply the promised matching non-Gaussian converse. The central within-N_n mixture-close lower experiment remains new unsolved mathematics, so the field-level Pareto-frontier kernel was not delivered.
tldr: For a primitive JMS partially linear law and fixed training-realized nuisance fits supplied within stated \(L^8(P_X)\) radii, one interval is honest over exact-Gaussian and shrinking fourth-cumulant-separated branches of the projected evaluation experiment. Four explicit Bonferroni-calibrated median-of-means events use nonempty finite-sample block partitions and cover safe DML, four residual moments, centered Appell inversion, and its empirical slope. The non-Gaussian finite-sample length is \(\min\{d_n,B_n/\delta_n+d_np_{\mathrm{sel},n}\}\), with an explicit bound on \(p_{\mathrm{sel},n}\), and reduces to \(\min\{d_n,B_n/\delta_n\}\) when \(\delta_n/s_n\to\infty\). On supplied-fit sequences satisfying the stated conditional-transfer compatibility, the certified Gaussian lower coordinate is \(d_n^-\): the nuisance-product/log term comes from the transferred support-localized JMS fuzzy construction, while \(n^{-1/2}\) comes from a separate compatible two-point family proved inside the present class. The literal full-class statement of JMS Theorem 3.2 is not used for this sum because its bounded-\(Y\), full-support Gaussian-treatment conditions force slope degeneracy under conditional outcome orthogonality, and its displayed root-\(N\) witness has unbounded Gaussian outcome. Conditional outcome-noise nondegeneracy is confined to the lower subexperiment. The within-non-Gaussian or constrained-risk branchwise converse and removal of the Gaussian logarithm remain open; no matching Pareto frontier or global union-supremum improvement is claimed.
gap: Published structure-agnostic PLM theory and the sibling repository paper study separate Gaussian or fixed-non-Gaussian point-estimation classes and fixed-separation spectral constructions, not one conditionally specified projected experiment with union honesty, shrinking cumulant separation, and branchwise expected length.
fill: The proved component combines explicit nonempty-block four-event calibration, a finite-sample branch-selection error envelope, a safe unnormalized DML interval, and a fully centered split Appell inversion for the shrinking-separation upper frontier. Conditional outcome-noise nondegeneracy is auxiliary to the Gaussian expected-length lower theorem, and the PLM-compatible fuzzy-Hermite converse remains open.
